purpose: Classify 2024–2026 freshness leads without confusing recent publications with new theory origin dates.

candidates.title: Wavefunction matching for quantum many-body problems
candidates.reason: The Nature paper explicitly introduces a named computational approach, and Quantum Index already treats distinct many-body computational frameworks as first-class entities.
candidates.nextAction: Add as a 2024 computational framework in a separate census PR after identity and relationship review.

candidates.title: Noninvertible symmetry frameworks
candidates.reason: The 2024 quantum-operation connection is new, but noninvertible symmetry research predates 2024; do not assign a false 2024 origin year.
candidates.nextAction: Run a separate origin/identity audit before deciding whether the broader framework is missing from the catalog.

candidates.title: DESI dark-energy constraints
candidates.reason: These are major observational updates affecting existing cosmological models, not newly invented theories.
candidates.nextAction: Represent as dated DevelopmentEvents and later Evidence records.

candidates.title: LZ extended recoil candidate
candidates.reason: A 2.6-sigma global excess is a candidate event/constraint, not a new dark-matter framework or a discovery.
candidates.nextAction: Represent as DevelopmentEvent now and an Evidence object in the evidence pilot.

candidates.title: Genuine quantum scars in many-body spin systems
candidates.reason: The 2025 result broadens an existing quantum-scar framework; the framework itself predates 2025.
candidates.nextAction: Represent as a DevelopmentEvent linked to scars, ETH and quantum chaos.

candidates.title: Recent emergent/topological gravity proposals
candidates.reason: Recent individual proposals do not yet establish a distinct durable first-class framework without a stronger identity and literature lineage review.
candidates.nextAction: Revisit during the quantum-gravity candidate census; do not add solely to populate recent years.
